title: Unified Inference: product overview, PRD, design, roadmap, pricing & release notes
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This document consolidates the product overview, high-level PRD (requirements), design/architecture notes, roadmap & themes, pricing and packaging guidance, and the initial release notes for the Unified Inference product suite. It is intended for engineering, product, sales, and customer-facing teams who need a single reference for feature scope, success criteria, and rollout plan.

Goals (product-level)

- Provide a unified runtime and API that enables consistent LLM inference across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Deliver measurable cost and latency improvements vs baseline customer deployments (target: 30% lower per-token cost at parity latency for common workloads).
- Make model routing, caching, and quantization recommendations first-class to reduce ops burden.
- Ship a pricing & packaging model that clearly maps to customer economics and ramps revenue for Dedicated and Private.

Success metrics (first 12 months)

- Adoption: 50 enterprise customers on Dedicated or Private plans; 2,000 active Hosted API customers using unified inference routes.
- Performance: median p95 tail latency <= 250ms for short-text generation (<= 256 tokens) on Dedicated.
- Cost efficiency: average token cost reduction of 25-40% vs naive single-request serving baseline using smart batching + KV caching.
- Reliability: platform SLOs at 99.95% availability for Dedicated; 99.9% for Hosted.

Target users and personas

- Product engineers building chat and assistant features (latency-sensitive).
- ML Platform teams who need predictable throughput and observability.
- Security/compliance teams evaluating Private deployments (VPC / on-prem).

Scope and product components (summary)

1) API & SDK surface (Hosted + Dedicated + Private)
- Text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking endpoints.
- Streaming API and function/tool-calling semantics.
- Route-level configuration (model, batching policy, cache policy).

2) Serving runtime & optimizations
- Continuous batching, KV/prefix caching, kernel selection, quantization profiles.
- Model variant routing (accuracy vs cost trade-offs).

3) Console + Observability
- Per-route latency/cost breakdown, token-level traces, quality regression alerts.

4) Pricing & packaging
- Hosted: usage-based per-token/embedding with tiered discounts.
- Dedicated: reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits + overage model.
- Private: license + deployment support + optional managed services.

PRD: Requirements and prioritized backlog

Top-level user stories (must-have)

1. As an application engineer, I can pin a route to a model variant and set a latency SLO, so the platform guarantees fallback behavior when capacity is constrained.
2. As an ML platform engineer, I can configure batching and cache policies per route and see per-token unit economics.
3. As a security reviewer, I can request a Private deployment package with KMS integrations and audit logging.
4. As a product manager, I can see model-level quality regressions tied to a canonical prompt set.

Non-functional requirements

- Performance: p95 <= 250ms for short-chat generation on Dedicated for target models; p95 <= 500ms for Hosted.
- Scalability: support 10k RPS aggregate in a Dedicated pool for a single customer with autoscaling to 20k RPS burst.
- Multi-tenancy: logical isolation for Hosted; physical and network isolation for Dedicated and Private.
- Security: support customer-managed KMS, VPC peering, and audit log export (S3/CloudWatch).

Priority roadmap (M0-M6)

- M0 (now): Core API parity with existing Redwood API + unified route abstraction.
- M1 (1 month): Batching + basic KV cache + route config UI.
- M2 (2 months): Model variant routing + kernel selection heuristics + quantization profiles.
- M3 (3 months): Dedicated capacity beta with SLA and reserved pools.
- M4 (4 months): Private deployment docs + onboarding checklist + KMS integration.
- M5 (5-6 months): Release v1 pricing & packaging, quality monitoring, and rollout to GA.

Design & architecture notes

High-level architecture

- Control plane: route configuration, policy engine, billing hooks, and console.
- Data plane (serving runtime): batching layer, KV cache, model workers, kernel selector, and telemetry exporter.
- Orchestration & scaling: autoscaler per-customer pool, fallbacks to compatible model variants, and cross-region routing.

Key design decisions

1. Continuous batching at the front of the runtime to maximize GPU utilization while honoring latency SLOs.
2. Multi-tier caching: in-memory request prefix cache (hot tokens) + persistent KV for common prefixes across sessions.
3. Kernel selection: runtime will choose FP16/INT8 kernels and fallback to FP32 for accuracy-critical routes. Kernels selected based on sequence length distribution and hardware capabilities.

Operational concerns and runbook highlights

- Latency spike investigation checklist: check autoscaler metrics, batch size distributions, KV cache hit rate, and model worker OOMs.
- Rollback strategy: immediate route-level downgrade to lower-cost model variant + autoscale increase for burst capacity.

Requirements table (condensed)

Requirement ID | Title | Priority | Acceptance criteria | Owner
--- | --- | ---: | --- | ---
R-001 | Route-level latency SLOs | Must | Configurable SLO + automated fallback when SLO violated | Runtime team
R-002 | Per-token billing breakdown | Must | Console shows cost per route per hour and per-1000 tokens | Billing team
R-003 | Dedicated reserved pools | Must | Reservation API + SLA 99.95% | Eng infra
R-004 | Private VPC deployment | Should | On-prem/or VPC image + install guide + KMS support | Private deploys

Roadmap & themes (next 12 months)

Quarterly themes

- Q1: Platform parity & Dedicated beta (runtime stability, batching, console).
- Q2: Cost controls (quantization profiles, caching heuristics, intelligent batching recommendations).
- Q3: Private deployments & compliance packages (SOC2 enhancements, KMS/HSM support).
- Q4: Ecosystem and partner integrations (cloud marketplaces, hardware partners).

Milestones and release cadence

- Beta release (M3): Dedicated beta with 10 pilot customers.
- GA v1 (M6): Hosted + Dedicated + Private core features + pricing & packaging live.
- v1.x (post-GA): Observability improvements, advanced routing policies, model-specific performance profiles.

Pricing & packaging notes (guidance for GTM and sales)

Principles

- Map price to economics: show customers estimated per-token costs and typical monthly bill ranges for benchmark workloads.
- Clear upgrade paths: Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private with credits applied for onboarding.
- Align discounts with commit terms for Dedicated (monthly vs annual) and seat/usage bands.

Suggested models

1) Hosted (self-serve):
- Pricing: per token generation (prompt + completion), embeddings billed per 1K vectors.
- Tiers: Free tier (developer), Standard (small teams), Business (discounted rate at volume).
- Add-ons: longer retention for observability, advanced eval tooling.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity):
- Pricing: base monthly reservation (vCPU/GPU pool) + overage per-token/unit.
- Commit discounts: 10% for 6-month, 18% for 12-month, custom for >$250k ARR.
- SLA: 99.95% uptime; credits applied per standard policy.

3) Private (license + services):
- Pricing: platform license (annual), deployment service fee, optional managed services.
- Compliance addons: SOC2 Type II evidence delivery, annual attestations, additional audit logging retention.

Example customer pricing vignette

- Mid-market SaaS doing chat: 100M tokens/month. Hosted cost estimate: $X/month (show sample calc in sales collateral). Dedicated reservation: $Y/month with 30% lower per-token cost after accounting for reserved GPU efficiency.

Packaging and SKU guidance

- SKU 1: Hosted-Core (API access, standard analytics)
- SKU 2: Hosted-Pro (higher QoS, longer retention, premium support)
- SKU 3: Dedicated-Base (1 reserved pool, standard SLA)
- SKU 4: Private-Base (license + install)

Release notes: v1.0 (planned GA)

Release date: Target M6 (approx. 2026-03-25)

Highlights

- Unified route abstraction across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Continuous batching with latency SLO enforcement.
- Basic KV/prefix caching with route-level controls.
- Dedicated reserved pools with beta customers and SLA.
- Console: per-route cost and latency breakdowns.

Known limitations in v1

- Kernel/quantization picks are conservative for uncommon model architectures.
- Private deployment automation requires manual steps for some on-prem network topologies.
- Quality monitoring is limited to basic prompt-set regression alerts; advanced model evaluation workflows are post-GA.

Rollout plan (operations)

1. Internal preview (Weeks 0-2): platform + SRE + solutions engineering smoke tests.
2. Pilot (Weeks 3-8): onboard 8-10 pilot customers (mix of mid-market + enterprise). Collect telemetry and iterate.
3. Early access (Weeks 9-12): expand to 50 customers, charge early-access fees, launch GTM materials.
4. GA (Week 16): open signups, enable Dedicated in selected regions, publish pricing.

Appendix: Operational checklists (shortened)

Incident: High p95 latency on Dedicated route

1. Verify autoscaler status and queue length (eng-sre dashboard).
2. Check median batch sizes and batch wait time distribution.
3. Measure KV cache hit rate and underlying model worker CPU/GPU utilization.
4. If congested: temporarily downgrade route to compatible lower-cost model variant; increase autoscaler target for burst capacity.

Install checklist for Private deployment (high level)

- Validate network connectivity and VPC peering requirements.
- Provision KMS/HSM credentials and test sign/verify flows.
- Run smoke suite: API connectivity, KV cache health, model worker inference correctness.
